title: Sketch
description: Sketch, in sketch cinematography, is line on paper before paint: searching contours, hatching in the shadows, reserved paper in the lights, a drawing that still looks. Unfinished is the look, and a clean vector portrait is not.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Process, memory, a story being invented: hands and eyes can be tighter than the room. Photographic structure sits underneath so it remains a shot of a person.
Canvas is paint. Sketch is the step before.
It is the wrong tool when you need finished oil, luxury-ad polish, or full animation. If there are no searching lines, it is an illustration, not a sketch.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Portrait distance, 50mm to 85mm, lock-off. Paper-white as the highlight, graphite or ink line, hatching in shadow.
Do not finish into a clean illustration. Prompt: Sketch treatment of [Subject], line, paper tooth, unfinished hatching, a drawing that still looks.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: A clean vector portrait, or a finished Canvas. The tell is no searching line.
Fix it: hatching, reserved paper, unfinished contours, a face that still looks.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Sketch in film?
A pre-paint recipe: line, paper tooth, unfinished hatching, a drawing that still reads as a person. Unfinished is required.
Sketch vs Canvas
Canvas is finished oil. Sketch stops at line and hatching. If you see bristle and wet lights, you wanted canvas.
When should I use Sketch?
Process, memory, invention. Skip luxury covers and finished gallery stills.
How do I prompt Sketch for AI image or video?
Portrait lock-off, then: Sketch treatment of [Subject], line, paper tooth, unfinished hatching, a drawing that still looks. Demand searching lines and reserved paper.
